question: Which guest scalar supplies the current displayed game year, and how is it updated from the turn number?

currentEvidence.method: foreground read-only Ghidra string, reference, and function queries followed by narrow generated-code corroboration

entries.role: calendar turn and year update function

currentEvidence.qualification: Static evidence establishes the converter, update flow, comparisons, and debug-format arguments. The default-off runtime probe matched the visible 1025 AD date at turn 61 and the visible 1050 AD date at turn 62.

calendar.converterResult: Starting at -4000, each positive turn advances by 100 while the year is negative, 50 while below 1000, 25 while below 1700, 10 while below 1900, 5 while below 1950, and 2 thereafter.
calendar.updateFlow: At 0x82D1EC3C..0x82D1EC50 the transition loads current turn, adds 1, stores low32, passes that exact value to 0x82CEFA20 and stores low32 year at 0x8312B8E0. Initialization has converter-derived paths; selected deserialization separately requests saved year and turn, so recomputation on every load is not inferred.
calendar.presentationCorroboration: 0x82E08CC8 passes 0x8312B8DC and 0x8312B8E0 as integer arguments to a diagnostic that formats pre-collection memory and RSX measurements followed by turn and year. The recorded format text is 61 UTF-8 bytes excluding terminator, SHA-256 692CEA47C800DFCABD6EB5C66D3B785AAE19A2E0FD51E8E19B3934EF07B80FE7; its original encoding is not established.
calendar.eventYearConsumer: Follow-on finding calendar-event-year-consumer proves that complete function 0x82DF9FD0 compares object field +0x444 with 0x8312B8E0 and immediately returns 1 when the years differ.
calendar.formatBoundary: Complete 0x82CF3920..0x82CF39B0 tests signed input r4 against zero, requests negative or positive magnitude formatting through 0x82E6A430 or selects a separate zero pointer, then requests 0x821B2AD8. The positive arm has no local 2100 clamp or year-indexed table. Descendant formatting and string allocation, which code is responsible for the main HUD, and final wording are not yet established.

runtimeProbe.result: On 2026-08-21 the owner observed Americans in the Medieval Era at 1025 AD; the probe reported civilization 7, era 1, turn 61, and year 1025. After one turn the owner observed 1050 AD; the probe reported turn 62 and year 1050.

staticQuery.truncationGuard: The maintained Ghidra program truncates the turn-transition and load functions after save-register thunks. Ghidra directly decompiles the converter and recovers scalar references of limited scope; generated code supplies the exact increment, converter call, and store sequence.
staticQuery.lateCalendarVerification: Fresh native converter 32 words, transition 6, formatter 37 and caller 8 matched image.json. Independent checks covered 277 late-curve inputs, four cap, prior, next and warning tuples and the first signed32 year-wrap pair. These are static results, separate from the earlier 1025 and 1050 runtime observation.

guards: Do not derive the displayed year independently from era; era and year are separate guest values.
Publish the calendar scalars only when the corresponding guest reads and the player-state check are valid.
Do not treat the retail debug formatter as runtime observation of a rendered UI string.
Do not assume AD wording for year zero until the owner-visible presentation is checked.
No completed display, save and load, peer agreement or arbitrary-turn correctness beyond 2100 is established by late-calendar arithmetic alone.
conclusion: Version 1.3 maintains the current turn at 0x8312B8DC and the visible calendar year at 0x8312B8E0. Static initialization and transition evidence is confirmed by the owner-observed 1025 AD to 1050 AD turn transition.

dependencies.use: Complete converter preset-independence and selected 32-bit year and turn load requests, with helper and delivery guards.
Selected start-year threshold search and initialization publication, with guards that the pointer and frame stay valid.

lateCalendar.completeConverter: All 32 instructions 0x82CEFA20..0x82CEFA9C contain only register and CR integer arithmetic and branches, with no memory access or call. Signed32 input <= 0 returns -4000. Positive input iterates once per turn. The 1800 and 1900 thresholds both choose 10-year increments; the merged schedule in calendar.converterResult is unchanged.
lateCalendar.speedAndScenario: No SPEEDMODE or scenario value is an input to this complete body. The same input turn has the same output year. The exact transition publication sequence has no speed or scenario transform. This does not establish sole writers, per-round cadence or absence of upstream or later changes.
lateCalendar.curve: Turn 118 gives 1950. For 118<=T<1073740967 the stored signed year is Y=2*T+1714. No 2100 or 2500 clamp or finite calendar table ends this path.
lateCalendar.witnessQualification: Warning values are arithmetic five-turn leads, not a selected deadline policy. Absolute turns are converter inputs, not elapsed turns from every scenario start. Finite values through 2500 fit signed16 and signed32.
lateCalendar.startDate: Accepted initialization 0x82D24F20..0x82D24F6C reads a signed16 record+0x3E year threshold and can increment a kept turn until conversion reaches it, excluding zero or <= -4000 thresholds. Scenarios can select the starting point without changing the converter curve; initial turn, record and frame identity, and whether they stay valid, remain premises.
lateCalendar.wrap: T1073740966 produces 2147483646; the next step at T1073740967 yields low32 word 0x80000000, stored and interpreted as -2147483648. PPC64 addi keeps upper bits, but cmpwi and stw consume low32. Subsequent signed tests select a negative-year band, invalidating the simple late curve. Input turns with signed low32 <= 0 separately return -4000. No unbounded arithmetic claim follows.
lateCalendar.cost: The converter loops once per positive input turn; this is a static linear-work observation, not a timing measurement.
lateCalendar.displayCaller: At 0x82DF7684 the chart-label function 0x82DF7648 calls the converter; 0x82DF7688 moves its return to r4 and 0x82DF7690 calls 0x82CF3920. Positive 2500 follows the same local formatter branch as 2100. A completed visible HUD or date update beyond 2100 remains unobserved.
lateCalendar.saveWidth: Reuse scenario-speedmode-movement.json: selected deserialization 0x82CC424C and 0x82CC42B8 asks 0x822D93E8 for four bytes into current year and current turn respectively. No 2100 or 2500 scalar-width cap is imposed there. Current virtual+4 delivery, complete save and load, byte order and coherent values that stay valid remain separate requirements.
lateCalendar.storedHistoryWidth: Generated-code lead, not a confirmed bug: 0x82CE62A0, 0x82CEB348 and 0x82CC75B8 use signed16 stored history turns before conversion, so turn 32768 would read as negative. Turn 393 fits. The writer and any truncation policy are not linked to these readers, so no actual history failure is claimed.
lateCalendar.consumerBoundary: No year-indexed table occurs inside the complete converter or formatter. This is not a complete accounting of year consumers across the image, the history schema, results and UI, or the supported-Unlimited domain.

dominationDates.question: Which calendar year is the earliest at which the palace-count Domination arm can be reached for a given minimum of elapsed turns?
dominationDates.elapsedTest: Signed currentTurn - startTurn >= 10 at 0x82D11264. The start turn is the word at 0x8312B8D8 and the current turn is 0x8312B8DC.
dominationDates.otherConditions: A nonzero palace count for the player, a palace count at least the total less the definition halfword +0x16 (0 when 0x82FFE7C4 bit 0x08000000 is set), and a nonzero 0x82CEEA50(1). The request is 0x82D02AB8(player, 1) at 0x82D11284. The palace formula and callers are in ai-civilization-elimination.json.
dominationDates.derivation: From start turn 0 and year -4000, each positive converter step adds 100 while the year is negative, so turn T <= 40 gives year 100 * T - 4000.
dominationDates.nonzeroStart: The earliest turn is startTurn + the minimum, passed through the converter, so a scenario with a nonzero start turn does not share the table. A start at turn 20 (year -2000) with the native minimum reaches turn 30, year -1000.
dominationDates.qualification: The dates are static arithmetic from the converter, not observed endgame dates. Changing the minimum would change only the elapsed-turn test: it does not raise a year limit, and the palace-count and enabled-victory checks still apply. No alternative minimum is selected by this finding.
